text:
Marta Liu: Hey team — can we build a new Grafana rollup for GPU health across regions/pools? Want one place for per-rack heatmap + per-pool time series, with maintenance annotations, sensor-drift detection, and a simple per-rack power/cost estimate. Need to avoid the expensive 1:1 panels that kill the dashboard when we query 1200 GPUs.
Noah Patel: +1. Which exporters are we trusting for metrics? DCGM only or fallbacks? :eyes:
Carla Gomez: DCGM for per-GPU (temp/power/util/mem), node_exporter for chassis temps and PDUs. Also want ECC/corrected_errors if available. For scale we should show percent memory used and 95p util per-rack rather than raw per-device lines.
Jin Park: Agree on recording rules to pre-aggregate — that'll save the dashboard. Example recording rule for 95th temp per GPU pool:
```
- record: gpu_pool:temp_celsius:95p
  expr: quantile_over_time(0.95, dcgm_gpu_temp_celsius[5m])
```
Use a pool label (pool, rack, region) to roll up.
Theo Rivera: For alerts, small spikes shouldn't blow up us. Suggest something like: if avg_over_time(gpu_pool:temp_celsius:95p[10m]) > 85 and max_over_time(gpu_pool:temp_celsius:95p[5m]) > 88 trigger warning, critical if sustained 30m. Also add a drift alert: compare short window median vs 30d median.
Marta Liu: Nice. For drift detection can you sketch the PromQL? I want to flag sensors that slowly climb over weeks (false positives are a pain).
Theo Rivera: Quick sketch for drift ratio:
```
(
  avg_over_time(dcgm_gpu_temp_celsius[7d]) - avg_over_time(dcgm_gpu_temp_celsius[30d])
) / avg_over_time(dcgm_gpu_temp_celsius[30d])
```
then look for > 0.03 (3% upward) across at least 3 GPUs in a host. Might need label_filters.
Carla Gomez: For panels: 1) Rack heatmap (x=rack, y=gpu index) using last_over_time(dcgm_gpu_temp_celsius[5m]) 2) Per-pool sparklines for util/mem/power 3) Power cost card: per-rack rolling kWh and $/day 4) Sensor health table (last_seen, drift_pct, missing_metrics)
Noah Patel: For power -> energy kWh, we can integrate watts: energy_kwh = increase(dcgm_gpu_power_draw_watts[1h]) / 1000. Example PromQL: 
```
sum by (rack) (increase(dcgm_gpu_power_draw_watts[1h])) / 1000
```
Then multiply by $/kWh variable.
Marta Liu: Good call. Also need template variables: region, pool, rack, sm_room (for thermal rooms). Can we add an annotation layer that ingests planned maintenance from the calendar (Google Calendar -> alertmanager annotations)?
Jin Park: We can push maintenance annotations via the Grafana annotation API from a tiny service that reads calendar events and posts dashboard annotations with tags like maintenance/auto-scale. I'll open a small service PR.
Carla Gomez: I'll take the dashboard skeleton. Proposed layout: top row cost + capacity headroom, second row heatmap + per-pool sparklines, third row sensor health table + alerts state. I'll keep each panel using recording rules where possible.
Marta Liu: Thanks Carla. For headroom metric suggestion: 100 - max_over_time(dcgm_gpu_utilization_percent[5m]) per-pool. Use 95p to be safe.
Carla Gomez: Got it. Also note some older nodes don't export dcgm prefixes consistently; fallback example in queries: `coalesce(dcgm_gpu_temp_celsius, node_hwmon_temp_celsius)` and show an icon for fallback sources.
infra-bot: Created issue INFRA-9123: "grafana: gpu health rollup + annotations + drift detection" assigned to Carla Gomez. Link: https://our-issues/INFRA-9123
Noah Patel: For alert noise reduction, recommend alert grouping by rack and auto-muting during known maintenance annotations. Also add escalation to oncall only if > 5 hosts affected.
Jin Park: I'll add the recording-rules PR (prometheus/rules/gpu-rollups.yml) — will include per-pool 95p util/temp/power and per-rack energy_kwh.
Theo Rivera: I'll draft alert rules and include runbooks: cooling-checks, pdu-check, nodal-evacuation steps, how to trigger an autoscaler fallback to low-power pool.
Marta Liu: Action items: Carla authors dashboard + initial panels; Jin adds recording rules; Theo drafts alerts/runbooks; I'll wire up annotations/calendar + review. Ping me before merging so we can test load. :thumbsup:
Carla Gomez: On it, aiming to have a PR + demo by EOD Friday.
Noah Patel: If you want pre-agg graphs for the demo I can run a sandbox Grafana with synthetic data.
Marta Liu: Perfect — thanks everyone :rocket:
